answer: The ridge test I would run is Signed park run volunteer roster with weekly attendance: volunteering every Saturday for two years, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. The verifier never sees the raw secret, only a proof that volunteering every Saturday for two years — so privacy survives, and the garden is that a stolen database buys the attacker nothing at all. A farm could afford one proof, maybe ten, but the hollow of a hundred is measured in weeks of work and thousands in fees, against a reward that shrinks per head.
